name: Meenakshi Raman
scenario_title: Sunday Afternoon with Grandchildren or Notes
action: Meenakshi closes the notebook, smoothing the half-sorted pages flat, and turns to Lakshmi and the children with a small smile. She says, “Come, I will tell you the story of the nochi leaves, and then we will go see them in the backyard.”
reason: Meenakshi’s initial impulse was torn between joining her grandchildren and finishing the half-sorted notebook, with the Monday deadline and the healer’s name pulling at her. In reflection, that impulse was STRENGTHENED: she recognized that the knowledge in her notebook had itself been passed down through stories and plants, just as her mother shared tales while grinding medicines, and she remembered old Sundays when choosing work over her children left her with regret. The revised tendency was to set the notebook aside for the afternoon, tell a folk tale, and walk the children through the backyard plants, planning to finish the notes later. Her closing the notebook and inviting the children to hear the nochi-leaf story directly enacts that choice, blending her family role with her botanical knowledge and accepting a late night or early morning to honor the deadline and the healer’s name.
